result.summary: Sell a fixed-scope GitHub Actions setup package to small dev teams that still repeat CI tasks by hand; the offer is narrow, easy to explain, and can be closed as a one-time setup plus support.
result.opportunity: Small engineering teams commonly configure the same CI tasks repeatedly—lint, tests, build, package, deployment notifications, issue labeling, or release automation—but many do not have a reusable, production-safe GitHub Actions workflow. The pain is visible in the repo, easy to measure in engineer hours saved, and suitable for a low-cost, fixed-scope setup service.
result.target_customer: Small software teams and agencies in Europe/Spain with 2-20 engineers, active GitHub repositories, and repeated CI tasks such as lint/test/build/deploy or release automation.
result.offer: A fixed-scope GitHub Actions setup package: repository audit, identification of one repeating CI task, creation of a reusable workflow, required secrets/config wiring, minimal documentation, and 2 weeks of support for rollout and fixes.
result.why_now: GitHub Actions is a mainstream CI/CD platform used to automate build, test, deployment and repository events; the public docs and marketplace show this is a real, active category. The buyer value is tangible: fewer manual minutes, faster PR validation, and fewer broken release steps. This makes it easier to sell than a broad SaaS or dashboard concept.
actions_completed: Reviewed playbook route #19 and compared it with newer local SEO/GBP and Shopify-feed attempts in the current pool.
Studied GitHub Actions docs to confirm the workflow model and the market category.

execution_packet.channel: Personalized email or LinkedIn message to engineering managers/founders of small GitHub-hosted software teams and agencies using public contact details from their repo or company site.
execution_packet.subject: GitHub Actions setup to remove repeated CI work
execution_packet.message:
Hola [Nombre],

He visto que vuestro repositorio ya usa GitHub y que el flujo de CI parece repetitivo para [lint/test/build/release]. Esto suele ser un buen punto para automatizar con un workflow reutilizable, en lugar de que cada PR o release se configure a mano.

Mi propuesta: un paquete fijo de 299 EUR para revisar el repo, identificar un trabajo repetido, crear un workflow reutilizable de GitHub Actions y dejarlo funcionando con documentación básica. Incluye una primera validación y 2 semanas de soporte para ajustes.

Si os interesa, puedo enviar un ejemplo mínimo de workflow para vuestro caso concreto y dejaros una propuesta clara sin coste de diagnóstico.

Referencia: RANK-IAMO499

Saludos,
IAMO499 / DesarrollAMO

(He incluido la referencia RANK-IAMO499 para atribución comercial en la propuesta y en la evidencia asociada.)
execution_packet.deliverable: One working GitHub Actions workflow for a single repeated CI task, YAML config file, environment variable checklist, repository setup notes, and a 2-week support window with one revision round.

result.differentiation_from_previous: I moved away from the saturated local-review/GBP and Shopify product-feed patterns and chose a tighter, lower-friction technical service: fixed-scope GitHub Actions setup for a real, measurable CI pain. This is more operationally valuable than generic SEO or review recovery and easier to explain in outcome-based terms: time saved, fewer manual steps, and more reliable release pipelines.
result.next_step: Identify 20 small GitHub-hosted software teams or agencies with visible CI pain, send one brief personalized message with a concrete workflow example, and if they respond, send a one-page sample and close the first 299 EUR setup via CobrAMO using reference RANK-IAMO499.
